Directing President Trump’s speech in Nebraska. Trump came to Grand Island on Monday to rally support for U.S. Sen. Pete Ricketts, Gov. Jim Pillen and Nebraska's Republican ticket. He also signed an executive order onstage that he said will lower diesel costs for truckers and farmers. It was Trump's first campaign stop in Nebraska since 2022 and part of a midterm swing through Republican-leaning states. Ricketts faces a challenge from independent Dan Osborn, who is backed by the Nebraska Democratic Party, while Pillen faces Democrat Lynne Walz. "With your support, just 29 days from now, Nebraska is going to defeat the radical left Democrats once again," Trump told the crowd at the Nebraska State Fair's Pinnacle Bank Expo Center. Trump also promised a payment to every adult citizen if Republicans keep Congress. "If Republicans win the House of Representatives and the Senate, I am going to give all adult citizens in the United States of America $5,000. And only Republicans can do that, and the Democrats can't, because we're taking in massive amounts of money through tariffs and record-setting economic success," Trump said. He said the money would have to be spent in the United States and called it a "Trump dividend" totaling $1 trillion. He did not say when it would be paid or whether Congress would need to approve it. videos.caption: President Trump on Tuesday announced a multibillion-dollar investment to build a new shipyard in Baltimore to manufacture critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class nuclear-powered attack submarines.   "Today, we're officially launching the construction of the largest new shipyard in the United States," he said at Sparrows Point Shipyard in Baltimore. "Since World War II, there's been nothing like we're doing today."   Anduril Industries, a defense technology company that makes AI-backed weapons, will invest $3.7 billion in the new shipyard, while the U.S. Navy has awarded the company a contract worth up to $2.9 billion to manufacture submarine components.   The shipyard is expected to create more than 3,000 new permanent jobs and support an additional 11,000 jobs across the nation.   The manufacturing facility will be located at the site of the former Bethlehem Steel plant, which closed permanently in 2012 after 125 years of steelmaking at the site.   "When I came into office for my second term less than two years ago, this national treasure was abandoned and it was totally forgotten. But it's not forgotten any longer," President Trump said.   The president also said the U.S. government will take a 40% stake in the new shipyard, demonstrating a commitment to the facility and Sparrows Point.   "The storied grounds of Sparrows Point will never fall silent again," he said. #cspan #trump #maryland #shipment #news
